The full suite passes: **44 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS** — including `Cp30Tests` (the new locality-postcode behavior) and `Cp17Tests` (unchanged city-fallback behavior).

## Summary

The locality derivation now prefers the postcode, falling back to the city.

**`Postcodes.java`** — added a reverse lookup `regionOf(String postcode)` that returns the region whose pinned range (NSW 2000–2099, VIC 3000–3099, QLD 4000–4099) contains the postcode, or `null` when the postcode is absent, unparseable, or in no known range. It reuses the existing `REGION_RANGE` table so the ranges stay defined in one place.

**`Localities.java`** — added an overload `of(String postcode, String city)` that resolves the postcode first via `Postcodes.regionOf(...)` and only falls back to the existing city-to-region lookup (`of(String city)`, kept intact and still used by `Postcodes.isValidForCity`) when the postcode yields no region.

**`OwnerMapper.java`** — the `locality` mapping now calls `Localities.of(owner.getPostcode(), owner.getCity())` instead of the city-only variant.

This returns the same region for a known city (e.g. Sydney → NSW) but disambiguates same-named cities: an unknown city with a VIC-range postcode (3000) now derives VIC, as the new `Cp30Tests` asserts. Postcode validation behavior is unchanged.
